IDEA: COOC_RANK_FRECHET
TITLE: Training co-occurrence barycentres in rank-based hyperbolic code assignment
MOTIVATION: Items co-consumed across a user’s training history may share useful semantic structure even when their encoder representations are not nearest in Euclidean space. Letting that structure participate directly in code selection may produce SIDs whose prefixes better support next-item prediction.
NOVELTY: The behaviour context is computed from current pre-quantisation representations of training co-occurrence neighbours, then hyperbolic proximity to that context contributes a candidate-code rank in the same assignment decision as reconstruction error. Neither the behaviour context nor the curved distance is an auxiliary loss.
CHANGE: Before Stage 2, build frozen symmetric, row-normalised co-occurrence rows from each user’s longest training sequence. During assignment, compute each item’s hyperbolic barycentre from its neighbours’ current encoder outputs, rank every candidate by Euclidean reconstruction error and by hyperbolic distance to that barycentre, and choose the code with the lowest sum of ranks.
SPECIFICATION: For training items \(i,j\), set \(C_{ij}=\sum_u \mathbf{1}[i,j\in S_u]\), counting each pair once per user’s longest training sequence; set \(W_{ij}=C_{ij}/\|C_{i,:}\|_2\) when the row is nonzero. At each assignment, let \(z_i\) be the current encoder output and \(c_k\) the valid, initialized code vectors. Compute the fixed-curvature (\(K=-1\)) Poincaré Fréchet barycentre \(b_i=\arg\min_{b\in\mathbb B}\sum_{j:W_{ij}>0}W_{ij}d_{-1}(b,z_j)^2\). For each code \(k\), compute \(e_{ik}=\|z_i-c_k\|_2^2\), \(h_{ik}=d_{-1}(z_i,b_i)\) if \(c_k\) is represented in the hyperbolic assignment space, and rank both quantities over candidate codes; choose \(k_i=\arg\min_k(r^e_{ik}+r^h_{ik})\). To make the behaviour rank code-dependent as required, use the code-conditioned point \(q_{ik}=\operatorname{Proj}_{\mathbb B}(z_i+c_k-b_i)\) and set \(h_{ik}=d_{-1}(q_{ik},b_i)\); this compares each candidate’s behaviour-context displacement rather than repeating the same distance for every code. Use ascending average ranks for ties and deterministic lowest-index tie-breaking after rank sums.
COST: Co-occurrence construction is a one-time sparse pass over training sequences. Barycentres cost \(O(\sum_i |\mathcal N_i| I)\) per assignment refresh for \(I\) fixed-point iterations; the extra candidate distances and ranks cost \(O(BK)\) per assignment step for batch size \(B\) and code count \(K\), plus sorting \(O(BK\log K)\). At the frozen scale (24 steps/epoch × 3000 epochs = 72,000 steps; 24,556 training items), the extra assignment work is repeated each step if assignments are refreshed each step; cache each item’s neighbour indices and recompute only its barycentre from current representations when that item is assigned. No extra trainable parameters are required.
HYPOTHESIS: The mechanism is worth keeping if the behaviour-conditioned curved candidate ranking changes assignments in a way that improves next-item SIDs, and the single frozen Stage 3 evaluation reaches test_recall@10 above 0.065. Record behavioural coherence, adjacency and transfer-predictability diagnostics alongside that result, but do not use them as admission gates.
RISKS: Neighbour representations may be noisy early in training; a barycentre may be poorly defined for widely dispersed neighbours; the behaviour rank may override useful reconstruction choices; and the additional per-candidate curved computations may increase Stage 2 time. The stated code-conditioned point is necessary to make the hyperbolic term vary by candidate; without it the behaviour rank is constant across codes and cannot affect assignment.
BEHAVIOR SIGNAL: Symmetric item co-occurrence in users’ training sequences.
BEHAVIOR COMPUTATION: Use only each user’s longest training sequence. Count every unordered pair of distinct items in that sequence once, symmetrise the resulting counts, and L2-normalise each item’s row. Freeze the sparse neighbour indices and weights before Stage 2.
LEAKAGE BOUNDARY: Construct \(C\) and \(W\) exclusively from the training split before Stage 2. Do not read validation or test interactions, including for sequence selection, neighbour construction, weight normalisation, or any assignment-time context.
HYPERBOLIC OPERATOR: Poincaré-ball Fréchet barycentre and Poincaré distance at fixed negative curvature \(K=-1\), with projection onto the open unit ball.
HYPERBOLIC LOCATION: The barycentre is recomputed from current pre-quantisation neighbour representations during assignment; the curved distance scores each candidate’s context-conditioned point against that barycentre.
COUPLING PATH: Frozen training co-occurrence weights select the neighbours and weight their current encoder representations in the barycentre. That barycentre and each candidate code form \(q_{ik}\); its curved distance determines a candidate rank that is added to the reconstruction rank to select the SID.
COUPLING EQUATION: \(b_i=\arg\min_{b\in\mathbb B}\sum_j W_{ij}d_{-1}(b,z_j)^2;\quad q_{ik}=\operatorname{Proj}_{\mathbb B}(z_i+c_k-b_i);\quad s_{ik}=r_k(\|z_i-c_k\|_2^2)+r_k(d_{-1}(q_{ik},b_i));\quad k_i=\arg\min_k s_{ik}\). Here \(W_{ij}\) is the training-behaviour term and \(d_{-1}\) is the curved term. The candidate-dependent \(q_{ik}\) ensures the behaviour/geometry rank can change the selected code.
OBSERVABLES: With both switches on, record per-item SID changes, assignment rank contributions, and behavioural coherence, adjacency and transfer-predictability diagnostics; evaluate Stage 3 test_recall@10 under the frozen protocol. A toy graph wiring check should verify that changing neighbours can change assignments, and a batch check should verify nonzero context and gradients reaching selected codes. These are checks, not trained ablation arms.
ABLATION BEHAVIOR OFF: Wiring switch sets \(W_{ij}=0\) for all neighbours; define the behaviour rank as tied across candidates, so selection reduces to the reconstruction ranking. Do not train this arm.
ABLATION GEOMETRY OFF: Wiring switch replaces the Poincaré barycentre/distance/projection with Euclidean weighted mean, Euclidean distance and unconstrained addition in the same candidate-conditioned formula. Do not train this arm.
ABLATION BOTH ON: Use the frozen training-only co-occurrence rows, current-representation Poincaré barycentre, candidate-conditioned curved distances and fixed equal rank sum. Train this candidate once, for the frozen 3000 Stage 2 epochs, then run the frozen Stage 3 protocol.
SPEC EQUATIONS: \(W_{ij}=C_{ij}/\|C_{i,:}\|_2\). If neighbours exist, \(b_i=\arg\min_b\sum_jW_{ij}d_{-1}(b,z_j)^2\); otherwise set \(r_k(h)=0\) for every code. For each candidate, \(q_{ik}=\operatorname{Proj}_{1-\epsilon}(z_i+c_k-b_i)\), \(e_{ik}=\|z_i-c_k\|^2\), \(h_{ik}=d_{-1}(q_{ik},b_i)\), \(s_{ik}=\operatorname{averageRank}_k(e_{ik})+\operatorname{averageRank}_k(h_{ik})\). Assign the smallest \(s_{ik}\), breaking residual ties by code index. Keep the existing quantizer’s reconstruction/commitment training path for the selected code.
SPEC INPUTS OUTPUTS: Inputs are a training item’s current encoder representation \(z_i\), current valid code vectors \(c_1,\ldots,c_K\), and its frozen sparse training co-occurrence neighbours and weights \(W_{ij}\). Output is the selected code index \(k_i\), its SID, and optional rank diagnostics.
SAFEGUARDS: Initialise the codebook through the existing valid initialisation before the first assignment. Project encoder points and barycentre iterates inside radius \(1-\epsilon\) (for example, \(\epsilon\) derived from the dtype’s machine precision); clamp Poincaré distance arguments away from zero and the ball boundary. Use a fixed iteration/tolerance stopping rule for the barycentre, finite-value checks, and renormalise nonempty neighbour rows. Empty-neighbour items receive a tied behaviour rank and therefore use reconstruction ranking alone. Use average ranks for ties and a deterministic code-index tie-break; do not add usage balancing, Sinkhorn, tuned coupling weights, or tuned temperatures.
END IDEA
